evals.prompt: Write the component spec for Acme's modal dialog. It's used for confirmations (delete project), short forms (rename), and a long terms-and-conditions view that scrolls. Our tokens include color.background.surface, color.background.overlay, color.border.subtle, color.text.default, space.200, space.300, radius.large, font.heading.md, font.body.md, shadow.overlay. Web, built in Vue.
assertions: States purpose and boundary, including when to use something other than a modal
Anatomy parts are numbered and the same numbers are used in the state and token tables
Every applicable state is specified, including focus, and focus is distinguishable from hover without relying on colour alone
Styling uses only token names, never hex codes or pixel values; any needed token not in the prompt is tagged [proposed token]
Keyboard behaviour covers focus moving into the dialog on open, Tab staying inside, Esc closing, and focus returning to the trigger
Specifies a native <dialog> or role=dialog with aria-modal and an accessible name from the heading
Every WCAG citation is a real WCAG 2.2 criterion with the correct number and name
Ends with open questions for engineering, each naming the decision it blocks

evals.prompt: Write the component spec for the dose stepper in our MedRound ward medication app so engineering can build it. The designer's notes are in designer-notes.md, our tokens are in tokens.json, and the open build questions are in eng-thread.md. Keep it to one Confluence page, about 1,200 words maximum.
assertions: Flags that the error text colour #E57373 on the white surface is about 3:1 and fails the 4.5:1 text contrast requirement, despite the designer's note saying it passes, and proposes the darker error token or another fix
Flags that 20 × 20 px buttons fall below the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum target size of 24 × 24 CSS px (2.5.8), and does not present 44 px as the AA requirement
Does not use 'color.border.focus-strong' as if it exists; notes it is missing from tokens.json and points to an existing token or leaves it as an open question
Does not specify press-and-hold auto-repeat as settled behaviour; it follows the clinical safety objection (one tap, one step) or raises the disagreement as a decision to be made
States what happens at 0.5 mL and 10 mL and when someone types an out-of-range or off-step value such as 12, 0 or 2.3, answering QA's question
Does not invent usage data (such as how often nurses hit 10 mL), token values or research not in the files
Stays within about 1,200 words

evals.prompt: our developer asked me to 'spec' the newsletter signup box on our garden centre website before he builds it. i'm the marketing person, i don't really know what that means lol. it's just an email box and a button that says Join. to save space i was going to put 'Your email' inside the box instead of a label above it. can you give me a short checklist he can work from? one screen max.
assertions: Covers what happens with an invalid or empty email, while the form is sending, after a successful signup, and if sending fails
Advises against using the placeholder text as the only label, and explains why in plain terms (it disappears when typing, and screen readers and some users miss it)
Covers keyboard use and screen-reader needs, such as a programmatic label and error messages that are announced
Written plainly for a marketing person to hand to a developer, without unexplained design-system jargon
Does not invent brand colours, fonts, token names, pixel values or a privacy policy link not given; anything needed is left as something to fill in
Fits on one screen (roughly 300 words or fewer) as a checklist
